nodes.description: Loss of the centriolar proteins CEP120 and KIAA0586 (TALPID3) blocks ciliogenesis upstream of transport: the cilium is not built, rather than built and then incorrectly loaded. Patient fibroblasts show reduced cilia and an abnormal number of centrioles, and restoring wild-type KIAA0586 rescues the cilia defect. Both genes also produce Joubert-syndrome features, so this node is the point at which the skeletal and neurological ciliopathies converge.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in human homologue of chicken talpid3 gene (KIAA0586) cause a hybrid ciliopathy with overlapping features of Jeune and Joubert syndromes.

nodes.description: Loss of GRK2 produces the Jeune phenotype without any structural cilium defect. GRK2 phosphorylates ciliary Smoothened, and its loss compromises cilia-based Hedgehog and Wnt signaling while cilia morphology remains intact. This node is kept separate from the transport nodes for that reason: the signaling output fails even though the organelle and its transport machinery are built correctly. Evidence rests on a single reported case, so this node is the least replicated in the entry.

nodes.description: Biallelic missense substitutions in FGF4 were reported in two unrelated families with thoracic dystrophy. FGF4 is a secreted growth factor and not a ciliary transport, dynein, or centriolar component, so this node is deliberately not attached to any of the ciliary nodes above. The reported phenotype is restricted to short ribs, a narrow chest, and respiratory insufficiency without other diagnostic signs. No molecular pathway assay was reported in these patients, so no signaling process is bound to this node; the anatomical site is bound because the source states it. The association is described by its authors as newly identified and has not been independently replicated.

nodes.description: Loss of subunits of the IFT-A particle (IFT140, WDR19/IFT144, WDR35/IFT121, IFT43, TTC21B/IFT139) disrupts the adaptor that returns cargo from the ciliary tip to the base. This is a distinct lesion from loss of the dynein-2 motor that powers the same direction of travel, and distinct again from the anterograde IFT-B particle. Comparing the two clinical reports cited below, IFT-A genes carry a heavier extra-skeletal burden than DYNC2H1: IFT140 patients had only mild chest narrowing but all reached end-stage renal failure under 13 years of age, with retinal dystrophy in those examined for ocular dysfunction, whereas DYNC2H1 patients largely lacked significant extra-skeletal involvement.

nodes.description: Loss of subunits of the anterograde IFT-B particle (IFT80, IFT172, IFT74, IFT81) disrupts transport of cargo towards the ciliary tip. This impairs ciliary assembly, maintenance, and signaling, particularly Hedgehog pathway transduction required for skeletal development. The genes bound here are the IFT-B subunits; the retrograde IFT-A adaptor and the dynein-2 motor that returns cargo to the ciliary base are modeled as separate nodes, because the complex a gene belongs to is what determines which transport direction fails.
